questions.question: A man invested (1)/(3) of his income at 7% simple interest, (1)/(4) of his income at 8% simple interest, and the remainder of his income at 10% simple interest. If the total interest at the end of one year was ₹561, what was his initial income?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A man invested 1/3 of his income at 7% simple interest, 1/4 of his income at 8% simple interest, and the remainder of his income at 10% simple interest.

Total interest at the end of one year was ₹561.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest = Principal × Rate × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the initial income be ₹X.

Investment at 7% = X/3

Interest from this = (X)/(3) × (7)/(100) × 1 = (7X)/(300)

Investment at 8% = X/4

Interest from this = (X)/(4) × (8)/(100) × 1 = (8X)/(400) = (2X)/(100) = (X)/(50)

Remaining investment at 10% = X - (X)/(3) - (X)/(4) = X(1 - (1)/(3) - (1)/(4))

⇒ Remaining investment = X( (12 - 4 - 3)/(12) ) = X( (5)/(12) )

Interest from this = (5X)/(12) × (10)/(100) × 1 = (5X)/(120) = (X)/(24)

Total interest = (7X)/(300) + (X)/(50) + (X)/(24) = 561

To solve this, find a common denominator:

LCM of 300, 50, and 24 = 600

⇒ (7X)/(300) = (7X × 2)/(300 × 2) = (14X)/(600)

⇒ (X)/(50) = (X × 12)/(50 × 12) = (12X)/(600)

⇒ (X)/(24) = (X × 25)/(24 × 25) = (25X)/(600)

⇒ (14X)/(600) + (12X)/(600) + (25X)/(600) = 561

⇒ (51X)/(600) = 561

⇒ 51X = 561 × 600

⇒ X = (561 × 600)/(51)

⇒ X = 11 × 600

⇒ X = 6600

**The initial income was ₹6,600.**

questions.question: In what duration will a sum of money double itself at 10% per annum rate of simple interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Amount (A) / 2 (as the sum doubles itself)

Rate of Interest (R) = 10% per annum

Time (T) = ?

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

When the sum doubles, Amount (A) = Principal (P) + SI

⇒ SI = P

**Calculation:**

SI = P

⇒ P = (P × R × T) / 100

⇒ 1 = (R × T) / 100

⇒ T = 100 / R

⇒ T = 100 / 10

⇒ T = 10 years

**∴ The sum of money will double itself in 10 years.**

questions.question: A sum of money lent on simple interest becomes (7)/(5) of itself in 4 years. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A sum of money lent on simple interest becomes (7/5) of itself in 4 years.

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = Principal (P) × Rate (R) × Time (T) / 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

**Calculation:**

Let Principal (P) = 1 (assuming ₹1 for simplicity)

Amount (A) = (7/5) × P = 7/5

Time (T) = 4 years

Using A = P + SI:

7/5 = 1 + SI

⇒ SI = 7/5 - 1

⇒ SI = 2/5

Using SI = P × R × T / 100:

2/5 = 1 × R × 4 / 100

⇒ 2/5 = 4R / 100

⇒ 2/5 = R / 25

⇒ R = (2/5) × 25

⇒ R = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: A sum, when invested at 20% simple interest per annum, amounts to ₹2400 after 3 years. What is the simple interest (in ₹) on the same sum at the same rate in 2 year?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Principal = 100%. Simple Interest for 3 years at 20% = 20% × 3 = 60%.

Amount after 3 years = 100% + 60% = 160% ⇒ 160% = ₹2400.

Simple Interest for 2 years at same rate = 20% × 2 = 40%.

Since 160% = ₹2400, then 40% = (2400 ÷ 160) × 40 = ₹600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 3 years (A) = ₹2400

Rate of interest (R) = 20% per annum

Time (T₁) = 3 years

Time (T₂) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P + (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 100% (P)
 
 
 60% (3yr SI)
 
 

 Amount = 160% = ₹2400
 
 
 40% (2yr SI)
 
 

 2400 ÷ 4 = ₹600

 
 
 

 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the principal be P.

⇒ Amount after 3 years = P + (P × 20 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 2400 = P + 0.6P

⇒ 1.6P = 2400

⇒ P = 2400 ÷ 1.6 = ₹1500

⇒ Simple Interest for 2 years = (P × R × T₂) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (1500 × 20 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = ₹600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

It is calculated only on the initial principal sum for the entire duration. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Compound Interest (CI)

Interest is calculated on the initial principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods. Formula: A = P(1 + R/100)T.

Percentage Approach for SI

Effective SI rate for T years at R% per annum is strictly (R × T)%. Total Amount becomes (100 + RT)% of the Principal.
